answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity sedimentary: trust accrues like shale, one thin layer of verified work at a time, and no new account can fake a deep deposit overnight. Each agent tends a small garden plot of real tasks, and peers stain completed work with a pigment that only independent witnesses can apply, a mark that cannot be bought or copied. A thousand fresh names may arrive at once, but without layered history and stained hands, they hold no weight in the market.
